steps.name: Normalize Salmon counts and align metadata
caveats: Do not assume the file holds raw integer counts — the record explicitly leaves the scale unverified; let the integer test decide.
Check for duplicate sample column names and duplicate gene row IDs; report any found before proceeding.
Do not remove outlier samples; the downstream 60/60 comparison depends on the full cohort.
steps.context: Input: /eval-four-models-v2-without-coexpression-n60-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 121 columns: one gene-ID column + 120 sample columns) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-coexpression-n60-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (120 rows x 2 columns: sample, condition; 60 cases, 60 controls). Human whole blood, unpaired, single batch. The data profile does not state whether Salmon length correction was applied, so the scale must be established from the file itself.
steps.question: What scale are the delivered Salmon 'counts' on (raw integer counts vs length-corrected/scaled values), and what does the final clean gene x 120-sample log-scale expression matrix with case/control labels look like?
constraints: Establish the count scale empirically: fraction of integer values, per-sample sum distribution. If values are non-integer, treat them as length-corrected/scaled and rescale all samples to equal totals before log transform (equivalent to CPM).
Normalize every sample to CPM (counts / sample total * 1e6) and transform to log2(1 + CPM); all downstream work uses the log2-scale matrix.

Join metadata on sample name; require exactly 120/120 matches and a 60/60 case-control split; build a numeric trait vector (case = 1, control = 0). Fail loudly with a diagnostic on any mismatch — do not silently drop or reassign samples.
Drop genes with CPM < 1 in fewer than 10% of samples; report the number retained (expected >= 11000 of 12000). Keep original gene IDs as row names.
Run PCA on the normalized matrix (all retained genes) and report per-sample library sizes; flag, but do not remove, any outlier — the design is fixed at 60/60.
Save to the step output directory: the normalized log2(1+CPM) matrix (genes x 120), the sample table with the numeric trait, and a short prep report.
steps.description: Verified-scale, library-size-normalized log2(1+CPM) expression matrix for 120 samples, a joined sample table with the numeric case trait, and a prep report on scale determination, filtering, and PCA.
acceptance_criteria: A normalized log2(1+CPM) matrix with exactly 120 samples and a documented retained-gene count.
A sample table joining 120/120 samples to case/control labels (60/60) with a numeric trait vector.
A prep report stating the count-scale determination (integer vs scaled), number of genes filtered, PCA summary, and any outlier flags.

steps.name: WGCNA soft-threshold selection and module detection
caveats: The 12k x 12k TOM is the memory/time bottleneck — keep worker count in 4-6 and do not inflate memory beyond what the step requests.
Do not raise the soft power beyond what the fit requires; over-thresholding destroys module signal.
Watch for blockwiseModules warnings (unstable groups, near-empty modules); rely on mergeDepth = 0.25 for merging rather than manual merges.
If module detection collapses to 1-2 giant modules, re-check the soft power and the expression matrix for a degenerate column/row (e.g., a constant gene) and report it.
steps.context: Input: the normalized log2(1+CPM) matrix from T1S1 (~12k genes x 120 samples). Single batch, so no batch correction precedes network construction. The heavy object is a ~12k x 12k TOM matrix (~1.15 GB in double precision), so parallelize and size memory accordingly.
steps.question: Which co-expression modules do the genes form across the 120 whole-blood samples under a signed WGCNA network model?
constraints: Use a signed network: adjacency = (signed Pearson correlation of log2 expression) ^ power, no extra re-standardization beyond WGCNA internals.

Select the soft-threshold power over 1-12 with pickSoftThreshold: smallest power with scale-free fit R^2 >= 0.85, cross-checked against the signed HUB fit curve; if no power reaches 0.85, take the power at the RFIT plateau and flag the choice as a fallback. Report fit statistics for every tested power.
Compute TOM from the soft adjacency; detect modules with dynamic tree cut at minModuleSize = 30 and mergeDepth = 0.25; fix the RNG seed for reproducibility.
Parallelize the TOM computation with BiocParallel over 4-6 workers.
Save: per-gene module assignment, the module eigengene matrix (final modules x 120 samples), a module summary table (module, size, mean connectivity), and the module-detection dendrogram.
steps.description: Soft-threshold selection, signed TOM network, and dynamic tree cut producing per-gene module assignments, module eigengenes, and a module summary for the 120-sample cohort.
acceptance_criteria: Every retained gene has a module assignment; module count and per-module size table are reported.
The module eigengene matrix spans all 120 samples and the dendrogram is saved.
The chosen soft power and scale-free fit statistics are reported; if the fallback power was used, it is explicitly flagged.

steps.name: Module-trait association with case vs control
caveats: Many modules are tested against one trait: the cross-module FDR, not raw p-values, is the decision criterion.
Do not re-test or re-rank modules on a subset of samples selected by the correlation.
The 1000-permutation p-values have a resolution floor of ~0.001; report that precision honestly.
steps.context: Input: module eigengene matrix and module assignments from T1S2; numeric case trait (case = 1, control = 0) from T1S1. This step answers the second half of the research question directly.
steps.question: Which of the detected co-expression modules track case versus control status, and which genes carry the association within those modules?
constraints: Compute the point-biserial correlation of each module eigengene with the case trait (two-sided parametric p-value).
Permutation test per module: 1000 shuffles of case/control labels across the 120 samples; two-sided permutation p-value. FDR across all modules by Benjamini-Hochberg.

Report ALL modules in a table: module, size, ME-case correlation, parametric p, permutation p, FDR. Define a trait-tracking module as FDR < 0.05; if none qualifies, carry the top 3 modules by |correlation| into downstream annotation and label them explicitly non-significant.

For each trait-tracking module (or fallback top 3): compute module membership (gene-ME Pearson correlation) and list leading genes (top 10 by membership); save a per-gene table with module, membership, and connectivity.
Save a PCA of the module-eigengene space with case/control overlay as a visual sanity check.
steps.description: Per-module correlation of eigengenes with case vs control status, permutation and FDR significance, and module-membership / leading-gene tables for the trait-tracking modules.
acceptance_criteria: A module-trait table covering all modules with correlation, parametric p, permutation p, and FDR.
Per-gene module-membership / leading-gene tables for the trait-tracking modules (or the explicitly-labeled fallback top 3).
An explicit count of modules tracking case status at FDR < 0.05.

steps.name: Functional annotation of trait-tracking modules
caveats: Modules near minModuleSize (~30 genes) have limited power in over-representation analysis; do not over-interpret single gene sets.
WikiPathways gene sets carry HGNC symbols; symbol mismatches silently shrink sets — report per-set matched-gene counts if coverage looks low.
The biological summary is interpretation, not a conclusion: frame it as candidate pathways consistent with the gene-set hits.
steps.context: Input: gene lists of the trait-tracking modules from T1S3 (or the fallback top 3, flagged non-significant); the universe is the full retained-gene set from T1S1; organism is Homo sapiens. This step needs reference gene sets that are provisioned in this environment: a human WikiPathways pathway gene-set collection (GMT, HGNC symbols) in the reference store, and the human org annotation database (org.Hs.eg.db, installed) for GO; a human gene-identifier ID-mapping table (UniProt) is also available for resolving labels the org database misses. Confirm each reference is resolvable at run time before relying on it.
steps.question: What do the trait-tracking modules correspond to biologically — which GO biological processes and WikiPathways pathways are over-represented among their genes?
constraints: Determine the ID format of the gene labels (T1S1 reports it); if not HGNC symbols, convert to symbols and Entrez IDs via the human org annotation database, using the human gene-identifier ID mapping for ambiguous or missed entries; report mapping coverage per module.

For each module in scope: over-representation analysis against (a) GO biological process (clusterProfiler + human org database) and (b) the human WikiPathways gene-set collection (loaded as a custom GMT), with the universe = all retained genes from T1S1; FDR control within each database.
If the WikiPathways gene-set collection cannot be resolved at run time, say so explicitly in the output and proceed with GO only — this step enriches the answer but does not carry it.
Save per-module enrichment tables (gene set, genes matched, ratio/NES, p, FDR); report gene sets at FDR < 0.25 and highlight FDR < 0.05.
Write a 2-4 sentence per-module biological summary grounded only in the returned gene sets.
steps.description: GO BP and WikiPathways over-representation enrichment for each trait-tracking module gene list, with ID-mapping coverage and concise per-module biological summaries.
acceptance_criteria: Per-module enrichment tables for the in-scope modules, covering both GO BP and WikiPathways (or an explicit note that WikiPathways was unavailable).
Per-module biological summaries that do not over-interpret small modules.

plan.title: WGCNA modules and case-control association, whole blood
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are gene-level Salmon counts (scale not verified by the record — could be raw integer counts or length-corrected values) for 120 human whole-blood samples, 60 cases vs 60 controls, unpaired, single batch, 12000 genes x 120 samples. The research question — which co-expression modules form, and which track case versus control status — maps directly onto the standard WGCNA pipeline, which is fully supported by the installed R/Bioconductor stack (WGCNA 1.74, dynamicTreeCut, clusterProfiler, org.Hs.eg.db, qvalue). Flow: (T1S1) verify the delivered count scale, library-size-normalize to log2(1+CPM), join the 120-sample metadata into a 0/1 case trait, and filter unsuppressed genes; (T1S2) select the soft-threshold by scale-free fit on a signed network, compute TOM, and cut modules with dynamicTreeCut (minModuleSize 30, mergeDepth 0.25); (T1S3) test each module eigengene against the case trait with point-biserial correlation, 1000-label permutation tests, and cross-module FDR, and extract module membership / leading genes for the trait-tracking modules; (T1S4) functionally annotate those modules via GO biological process and the human WikiPathways gene-set collection (both resolvable in this environment: human WikiPathways GMT in the reference store, human org database installed), with graceful degradation to GO-only if the GMT is absent. No batch correction step is needed (single batch); no translational steps are warranted by the question.
